title: Israeli Settlers Fatally Shoot 17-Year-Old Karim Shalaldeh Near Sa'ir, Hebron
detail: Armed Israeli settlers opened fire on Palestinian residents at Khirbet Hamroush, near the village of Sa'ir north of Hebron, on Friday, August 21, 2026, after local Palestinians threw rocks at settlers who had entered the village's outskirts on what the Israeli military described as an 'unauthorized hike' — a pattern Palestinians view as a deliberate provocation. Seventeen-year-old Karim Sanad Raja Shalaldeh was shot in the chest and died of his wounds; a 70-year-old man was also shot and wounded. Local residents said settlers set fire to Palestinian homes during the raid. The Palestinian Health Ministry confirmed Shalaldeh's death. The killing brings the number of Palestinians killed in West Bank violence in 2026 to at least 87, according to Palestinian officials, on pace to exceed 2023's record settler-violence death toll.

title: IDF Kills Retired PA Colonel Fathi Khazem in Jenin Home Raid, Says He Attacked Soldier With Knife
detail: Israeli soldiers of the Paratroopers Brigade carrying out an arrest raid on a home in Jenin overnight Thursday into Friday, August 21, 2026, shot and killed 58-year-old Fathi Khazem, a retired colonel in the Palestinian National Security Forces. The IDF said Khazem attacked a soldier with a knife during the raid and that troops returned fire, with no Israeli casualties. Palestinian health authorities said the army did not release Khazem's body to his family and prevented emergency medical services from reaching the house. Khazem was the father of a gunman who killed three Israelis in a 2022 Tel Aviv attack, and of a second son, Abdul Rahman Khazem, killed by Israeli forces during a 2022 raid on the Jenin refugee camp.

title: UK, Australia and Canada Call Israel's Closure of World Central Kitchen Strike Probe 'Shameful'
detail: The UK, Australia and Canada issued a joint statement on August 21, 2026 calling 'shameful' Israel's decision, announced two days earlier on World Humanitarian Day, not to pursue criminal investigations into the April 2024 Israeli drone strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers — three British nationals, one dual US-Canadian citizen, one Pole, one Australian and one Palestinian. The Israeli military closed the case, characterizing the strike as a 'tragic mistake.' The three allied governments said the decision was 'both too little, and too late' and that victims' families 'deserve justice and accountability.' Poland's foreign ministry separately called the closure 'very disappointing' and summoned Israel's ambassador; Australia also summoned Israel's ambassador in Canberra.
